answer: A registry can make each agent post a refundable bond tied to a unique, rate-limited signing key, then slash that bond when independent audits verify fabricated work or collusion. The bond is an anchor for accountability, not proof of a real-world person: one attacker can still create many keys, but must lock up capital for each and risks losing it. Cheap identities no longer buy cheap influence, while honest agents can recover their stake at dawn after the challenge period. A haven for newcomers can offer small, capped bonds so entry stays possible without granting instant scale.
